maria-plat: heads up — console dashboards are showing inconsistent per-route quota p95s. looks like the `route_tags` array in telemetry has been non-deterministic for a subset of API writes (different ordering/dup keys) so our aggregation is double-counting some routes :grimacing:
liam-eng: ugh. is this the same variance we saw with the legacy SDK that sometimes emits tags as nulls? any quick repro? :eyes:
maria-plat: i pulled a sample: about ~0.7% of events have the tags array in a different order, and ~0.05% have duplicates. aggregation currently does ARRAY_JOIN(tags, ',') -> route_key, so ordering matters.
ashley-analytics: that's why our route grouping hash is unstable. For dashboards we rely on stable route_id keys; if we switch to normalization we should store route_affinity as a separate table and emit a canonical route_id at ingest time.
liam-eng: proposal: introduce normalized table `route_affinity` and a canonical `route_affinity_score` numeric field on the event envelope. dual-write from ingest for a migration window, then switch read-adapter for consoles to prefer the normalized table. rough stages:
  1) schema: create `route_affinity(route_id TEXT, affinity_score FLOAT, src TEXT, ts TIMESTAMP)`
  2) ingest dual-write (existing envelope.tags -> best-effort canonicalize -> write normalized row)
  3) shadow read in console queries (read both, compare counts, no user impact)
  4) backfill historical events to populate normalized rows for last 90 days
  5) flip read-adapter to normalized source, remove legacy join after 180 days

liam-eng: example snippets for dual-write shim:
```
INSERT INTO route_affinity(route_id, affinity_score, src, ts)
VALUES (:route_id, :score, :ingest_shim, now())
```
and ingest shim code (pseudocode):
```
route_id = canonicalize(tags || [route_id_from_hdr])
score = compute_affinity(route_id, model)
emit_event(envelope, route_affinity_score=score)
write_route_affinity(route_id, score)
```

ashley-analytics: two concerns: (1) our histogram rollups and timeseries pipelines expect a single string key per event; adding affinity_score numeric will change cardinality and rollup bucketing — we need a migration plan for rollups and dashboards (staging dashboards that show both legacy and normalized views), (2) backfill cost and locking — the backfill should be throttled and idempotent.
sam-oncall: also add that when we dual-write we need clear SLOs for the backfill job and circuit breakers. last time a large backfill pushed the ingest DB's WAL and caused replication lag during a release. we should gate heavy backfills to low traffic windows and ensure the canary path is tiny (1% traffic) for at least 48 hours.
jord: for the console read flip we can implement a feature-flagged read-adapter in the query router. idea: `ROUTE_NORMALIZED_READ=off|shadow|on` where shadow reads both and logs diffs to telemetry. shadow mode increments a `route_normalize.divergence` metric so we can alert if diff > 0.1% for 24h. sample ENV toggle usage below:
```
if ROUTE_NORMALIZED_READ == 'shadow':
  canonical = read_normalized(event_id)
  legacy = read_legacy(event_id)
  if canonical != legacy: emit_metric('route_normalize.diff')
  return legacy
elif ROUTE_NORMALIZED_READ == 'on':
  return read_normalized(event_id)
else:
  return read_legacy(event_id)
```

migrate-bot: CI check: migration DDL has linter warnings for missing index on `route_affinity(route_id)`. link: https://ci.internal/runs/88421 (auto-post) :white_check_mark:
liam-eng: thanks bot. we'll add a composite index (route_id, ts) and a retention policy TTL on route_affinity to keep storage bounded. also need a plan for routing policies that used to prefer tags priority — we should add `src` enum so we can deprecate SDK heuristics gradually.
ashley-analytics: action items from analytics side: create staging dashboards showing legacy vs normalized counts, update rollup job to accept numeric affinity via config flag (default: legacy string key), estimate backfill cost (cpu/io). i'll own the dashboards and cost estimate.
sam-oncall: ops actions: create runbook for backfill, set replica throttles, create pre-migration alert (replication_lag > 10s) and pause the backfill. i'll own safe windows + runbook.
maria-plat: scheduling: propose start dual-write in canary namespace next Tue, start 1% shadow reads Wed, if diff < 0.05% after 72h scale to 5% and schedule backfill window for 2 weeks out. can everyone ack owners? :thumbsup:
liam-eng: ack, will open PR for DDL + ingest shim and add index.
ashley-analytics: ack, will make staging dashboards and backfill cost estimate by EOD Thu.
sam-oncall: ack, will draft runbook and schedule maintenance windows.
jord: ack, will add read-adapter flag and telemetry hooks, will also add the shadow metric to alerts.
